name: South Fork Flambeau River
gaugeName: SOUTH FORK FLAMBEAU RIVER NEAR PHILLIPS, WI
blurb: The South Fork Flambeau River through Price County toward the Flambeau River State Forest: quiet water, rapids and small dams.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.difficulty: Rapids and small rock dams (see DNR guide)
sections.notes: Start at the agency-listed Forest Road 144 access and finish at Smith Rapids. The guide’s Round Lake dam portage is upstream of this put-in. Scout the takeout near the covered bridge before launching; do not continue into Smith Rapids unintentionally.

notices.title: Rapids and rock dams
notices.text: Fish Trap, Little Bull and Riley Creek hazards precede Smith Rapids. Consult DNR page 14.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Paddle the Flambeau River, printed page 14

sections.routeReview: The available river line cuts across a present-day bend near Smith Rapids. Dotted geometry remains under review; exact landing and rock-dam approaches are not mapped.

sections.difficulty: Class I–III rapids marked in DNR guide
sections.notes: This reach ends at the Cedar Rapids bridge before the downstream Sugar Bush dam reach. Arrange your shuttle and confirm both bank approaches. This is a whitewater trip, not a casual tubing recommendation.

notices.title: Smith, Natural Dam and Cedar rapids
notices.text: Consult the DNR guide and scout conditions. These access areas do not identify a safe line through the rapids.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Paddle the Flambeau River, printed page 14

sections.distanceReview: The DNR guide’s rough intermediate distances imply about 3 miles; the USFS 2004 forest plan lists FR 148–FR 149 as 4.8 miles, and the USGS source course measures about 4.65 miles. The 4.7-mile planning value is retained as preliminary. Trip-time estimates stay withheld.
sections.routeReview: The dotted line is a reviewed river-course overview. It does not identify safe chutes through Smith, Natural Dam or Cedar rapids, or exact landing connections. Timing and disputed planning mileage remain separate from the display.

sections.takeOut: South Fork Flambeau River Access — Town of Eisenstein #3028
sections.difficulty: Class I–III rapids marked in DNR guide
sections.notes: Whitewater from Smith Rapids to the East Road / Forest Road 132 access area, passing Natural Dam, Cedar and Sugar Bush rapids. DNR’s paddling maps document this river corridor and the public take-out. This is not a casual tubing trip. The 8.2-mile planning distance is preliminary; check flow, scout hazards and confirm both landings.

notices.title: Smith to East Road: whitewater and rock-dam hazards
notices.text: DNR marks Smith Rapids and Sugar Bush Pond Dam as Class III, with additional Class I–II rapids. Check current flow and scout; the access map does not recommend a chute or establish a carry over private ground. Finish at the signed East Road access.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Paddle the Flambeau River, printed pages 14–15

sections.routeReview: DNR’s paddling guide maps the Sugar Bush rock-dam reaches as Class II–III rapids. This map shows approximate access locations; it does not identify a safe whitewater line, exact landing connections or a legal carry. Scout and confirm current conditions before paddling.

sections.difficulty: Class III at Cummings Rapids (DNR guide)
sections.notes: A short whitewater reach from the public Fifield access near Highway 70 to the Highway 13 landing. DNR’s paddling guide identifies these bridges as access points and maps Cummings Rapids between them. The 2.1-mile planning distance is preliminary. Check flow and scout; short distance does not make this an easy float.

notices.title: Cummings Rapids: Class III
notices.text: Cummings Rapids lies below the Fifield launch and above Highway 13. DNR rates it Class III; the dam inventory also records a rockfill structure in this reach. Scout and assess current conditions. This map shows access areas, not a safe whitewater line or a verified portage.
notices.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Paddle the Flambeau River, printed page 16

sections.routeReview: DNR’s guide describes the Highway 70–Highway 13 paddling reach and marks Cummings Rapids as Class III. The Town of Fifield rock-dam record lies in this rapids corridor. This access review does not approve an exact chute or carry; no dotted course through the rapids is enabled.
